Signet Jewelers' fiscal second-quarter sales fell 0.5% to $1.528 billion as same-store sales rose 2.2% and adjusted profit jumped 36% to $2.19 a share.

The Kay, Zales and Jared parent closed 48 net stores since fiscal year-end; winding down its James Allen brand is cutting $60–$80 million from revenue, per its SEC filing. Signet raised full-year EPS guidance to $10.45–$12.15 and expanded its buyback authorization to $700 million.

Gold traded at $4,389.30 an ounce on the paper's verified close of 9 September, silver at $66.13, platinum at $1,841.00 and palladium at $1,335.00.

Palladium was the session's only faller of more than 1%, down 2.63%, in a market where its own bid-ask spread ran near 3.00% of the bid.

The RapNet Diamond Index held at 3,902.2 for a one-carat stone, unchanged since 7 September.
